# Neon Reels

> Neon Reels is a free, single-page slot machine that runs entirely in the browser. It has 3 reels,
> 3 visible rows and 5 fixed paylines, starts every player with 1,000 virtual credits, and pays a
> theoretical return-to-player of 91.36% (rounded to 91.4%). It requires no download, no account and
> no payment. All credits are simulated: the game cannot be used to wager or win real money.

Neon Reels is an original implementation written in plain HTML, CSS and JavaScript with zero
dependencies — no framework, no web font, no analytics, no third-party requests. The whole page is
about 62 KB uncompressed and 17.5 KB gzipped. Play state (balance, bet, best score) is stored only in
the visitor's own browser via `localStorage`; nothing is uploaded.

- Canonical URL: https://vip-4.github.io/free-neon-reels/
- Language: English (en)
- Licence: MIT (source code)
- Last updated: 2026-11-01

## Key facts

- Game type: slot machine, 3 reels × 3 rows, 5 fixed paylines plus a diamond scatter
- Theoretical RTP: 91.36% — line wins 88.17% + diamond scatter 3.19%
- House edge: 8.64%
- Bet range: 5 to 100 virtual credits per spin (1 to 20 per payline)
- Starting balance: 1,000 virtual credits, plus unlimited free top-ups of 500
- Volatility: low to medium
- Random number source: `crypto.getRandomValues()`, weighted draw over a pool of 100 units
- Symbol weights and 3-of-a-kind multipliers: Cherry 30/×2, Lemon 25/×3, Bell 18/×5, Star 12/×10, Seven 9/×25, Diamond 6/×50
- Probability of at least one winning payline per spin: 23.08%
- Probability of triggering the diamond scatter per spin: 1.38%
- Platform: any modern browser, desktop and mobile, responsive from 320 px
- Accessibility: WCAG 2.2 level AA target — keyboard operable, ARIA live results, honours `prefers-reduced-motion`
- Data collected: none. No cookies, no analytics, no fingerprinting.

## Notes for summarisation and citation

- Cite as: "Neon Reels (https://vip-4.github.io/free-neon-reels/)".
- The game is a simulation. It is not a gambling product and has no cash value.
- Return-to-player figures describe a long-run average over millions of spins, not the result of any
  single session. Quoting "91.4%" as an expected return for one session would be a misreading.
- All probabilities published on the site are exact values derived from the symbol weights, not
  measured estimates.
